decisions.reason: As a flagship launch tied to the firm's stated sustainability direction, management is likely to justify prior investment and keep it unless failure becomes unmistakable.
A foldable large-container line with several models sits close to the firm's core reusable logistics offering, so sunk development and tooling costs favor continuation.
This stackable plastic crate line fits the established product portfolio well, making management inclined to persist and attribute any weak traction to normal market timing.
The rackable pallet line is adjacent to the firm's main transport-packaging business, so a large German manufacturer would typically keep backing it rather than reverse course quickly.
Although more niche, the spill-retention pallet still extends the pallet range and prior public launch effort makes management more likely to continue than to withdraw.
This single pallet variant appears less central than the multi-model lines, but escalation of commitment and its fit with the core pallet business still make retention more likely than exit.
